questions.question: What is a materialized view?

options.text: A database object that stores the result of a query physically, unlike regular views which are virtual

questions.explanation: Materialized view: query result stored as a physical table. Regular view: just a saved query, executed each time. Materialized views trade storage for speed—pre-computed results, instant reads.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of materialized views?

options.text: Fast reads of pre-computed complex queries without re-executing expensive operations

questions.explanation: Materialized view advantage: complex aggregations, joins computed once, stored. Queries read stored result instantly. Perfect for: dashboards, reports, frequently-run expensive queries.

questions.question: What is the main challenge with materialized views?

options.text: Keeping them in sync with base tables—refresh strategies and staleness

questions.explanation: Challenge: data staleness. Base tables change, materialized view becomes outdated. Must refresh: on-demand, scheduled, or incrementally. Tradeoff between freshness and refresh cost.

questions.question: What are the refresh strategies for materialized views?

options.text: Complete refresh (rebuild), incremental/fast refresh (apply changes), on-commit refresh

questions.explanation: Refresh strategies: Complete (drop and rebuild—simple but expensive), Incremental (apply only changes—faster but complex), On-commit (refresh after each transaction—always fresh but overhead).

questions.question: What is incremental refresh for materialized views?

options.text: Applying only the changes from base tables since last refresh, not recomputing everything

questions.explanation: Incremental (fast) refresh: track changes to base tables (via logs), apply deltas to materialized view. Much faster than complete refresh for large views with small changes. Requires proper setup.

questions.question: When would you use a materialized view instead of a regular view?

options.text: When the underlying query is expensive and results are queried frequently but don't need real-time freshness

questions.explanation: Use materialized views when: query is expensive (complex joins, aggregations), queried frequently, slight staleness acceptable. Regular views: simple queries, always need current data, storage constrained.

questions.question: Which databases support materialized views?

options.text: PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, Snowflake, and many others

questions.explanation: Materialized views supported by: PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server (indexed views), MySQL (simulated), Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery. Implementation details vary. Check your database's capabilities.

questions.question: What is a common use case for materialized views?

options.text: Dashboard and reporting queries that aggregate large amounts of data

questions.explanation: Common use cases: dashboards (daily sales summary), reports (monthly aggregates), data warehousing (pre-joined dimension tables), search (pre-computed rankings). Anywhere expensive queries run repeatedly.

questions.question: How do materialized views differ from summary tables?

options.text: Materialized views are database-managed with built-in refresh; summary tables are manually maintained

questions.explanation: Materialized views: database manages storage, provides refresh mechanisms, query optimizer aware. Summary tables: you create table, write refresh logic, maintain manually. MV is more elegant when supported.

questions.question: What is query rewrite in the context of materialized views?

options.text: Optimizer automatically uses materialized view to answer queries on base tables

questions.explanation: Query rewrite: optimizer recognizes query can be answered from materialized view instead of base tables. Transparent to application—queries base tables, gets MV performance. Oracle, PostgreSQL support this.

questions.question: A data warehouse has a query joining 10 tables that takes 5 minutes. It runs hourly for reports. Best solution?

options.text: Create a materialized view refreshed hourly, reports query the materialized view

questions.explanation: Perfect MV use case: expensive query (5 min), runs repeatedly (hourly), staleness acceptable (hourly refresh OK). Create MV, schedule hourly refresh. Reports get instant results from pre-computed data.

questions.question: What is the storage tradeoff with materialized views?

options.text: Materialized views consume storage proportional to their result set size

questions.explanation: Storage cost: MV stores full result set. Large aggregations = large MV. Multiple MVs multiply storage. Consider: result size, number of MVs, refresh frequency. Balance performance gain vs storage cost.
